newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 23.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - June 23.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

A deal announced on Friday by News Corp, Telstra Corp and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) to rationalise their pay-TV interests is expected to force another merger attempt between Foxtel and Australis. But approval from anti-monopoly watchdog the ACCC is not seen a fait accompli, given one merger attempt has already been rejected.

Cigarette manufacturer Wills said on Monday the proposed legistlative resolution of legal and regulatory issues affecting the U.S. tobacco industry was a solution to a unique U.S. situation, and would not set a meaningful precedent for Australia. A settlement reached last week could force the U.S. tobacco industry to hike retail prices and load up on new debt, industry analysts say.

An independent report by Grant Samuel and Associates has found that Foster's A$625 million share buyback is expected to reduce the company's 1996/97 earnings by A$30.6 million as a result of higher interest costs, newspaper reports said.
ICI Plc announces details of sale of its holding in ICI Australia at 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT).

The sports cable TV joint venture of Liberty Media Corp. and News Corp.'s Fox Sports was in talks to buy a major stake in Cablevision Systems Corp.'s Rainbow cable unit for about $850 million, an industry source said Friday. The talks were continuing, with an agreement possible by early next week, the source said. The venture would buy a stake of about 40 percent in Cablevision's Rainbow Program Holding, the source said.

Horticultural group Arthur Yates and Co Ltd said on Friday it expected its full year profit before abnormals for the year to June 30, 1997 to be below the same period last year. The expected result followed poor trading conditions in May. Directors would review the final dividend in the light of the final result, Yates said in a statement.

Investors angry at what they see as an unfair plan to merge nickel producer QNI Ltd with Gencor Ltd's nickel division could scuttle the A$2.3 billion deal at a shareholders meeting, analysts and brokers said on Friday.
